html:
The Yoga Sutras are 195 short Sanskrit sayings on the practice of yoga, credited to Patanjali and put together around 400 CE. They are the classic statement of yoga as a way to still the mind.

The second saying defines the subject: yoga is the stopping of the turnings of the mind. When the mind is still, the self sees that it is separate from the body and from thought, and is free.

The text sets out a path of eight limbs: self-restraint, good habits, posture, control of the breath, drawing the senses inward, concentration, meditation and full absorption. Posture gets only a few words. It means a steady and easy seat for meditation.

Yoga practices are much older than the text. They appear in the Upanishads, and the Buddha and Mahavira learnt from wandering teachers of the same kind. Patanjali's words borrow from Buddhist writing of his time.

The Yoga Sutras were little read by about 1500. Vivekananda brought them back with his book Raja Yoga in 1896. The yoga of postures now practised around the world grew mainly from later hatha yoga and from 20th-century teachers in Mysore and Pune.
sum: The Yoga Sutras are 195 short Sanskrit sayings on the practice of yoga, credited to Patanjali and put together around 400 CE. They are the classic statement of yoga as a way to still the mind.
